typicalChallenges: How do DR procedures maintain security controls during failover (encryption, access controls, logging)?
What is the security posture of the DR environment — is it as hardened as production?
How are secrets and credentials managed across primary and DR sites?
Could a DR failover be triggered maliciously and what controls prevent this?
How frequently are DR procedures tested and what was the result of the last test?
What is the actual measured recovery time versus the stated RTO target?
How many team members can execute the DR procedure and what happens if they are unavailable?
What monitoring confirms that DR replication is functioning correctly?
How does the DR architecture affect deployment complexity and frequency?
What additional testing is needed to validate DR capability after each release?
How are database schema changes propagated to DR environments?
Does the DR architecture constrain technology choices or deployment patterns?
What is the cost of maintaining DR infrastructure that may never be used?
How does the DR strategy (active-active vs pilot-light vs backup-restore) affect ongoing costs?
What is the business cost of downtime that justifies the DR investment?
Are there more cost-effective DR approaches that still meet the RTO/RPO requirements?
